commentary: Today, DCE iron ore conƟnued to weake trend today, with the most-traded contract I2601 closing at 788.5 yuan, down 0.32% from the previous trading day. Traders demonstrated a moderate willingness to sell, while steel mills purchased as needed. Overall market trading senƟment remained subdued. In Shandong, transacƟon prices for PB ﬁnes ranged between 785-790 yuan, down 0-2 yuan/mt from yesterday’s levels; in Hebei, transacƟon prices for 60.8% PB ﬁnes stood at 793-797 yuan/mt, down 2-3 yuan/mt from the previous day. Due to extended maintenance at steel mills, total producƟon of major steel products remained high this week. Although apparent consumpƟon saw a slight rebound and port inventories edged lower, current steel inventory levels remained elevated on a YoY basis, leading to widespread pessimism in the market regarding future inventory pressure on steel mills. Against this backdrop, iron ore prices remained under pressure and traded in the doldrums. However, as hot metal producƟon did not decline as expected, actual demand conƟnued to provide some support to ore prices, limiƟng further downside room. Looking ahead, given expectaƟons of a weakening fundamental outlook for iron ore, ore prices are expected to remain under pressure and exhibit a ﬂuctuaƟng trend.
